text: The monthly total in Model!C16 stops one row short, so the Contractors line of 375,000 is never counted, and the same gap repeats in all six month columns. Your costs therefore look smaller than they are, and everything built on those totals shifts with them: gross margin reads 0.084291 when it should read 0.012452, and the number of expensive months shows 4 rather than 6. Anyone reading this file would conclude your spending is lower and your margin healthier than the corrected figures show.
system: You explain spreadsheet defects to finance and operations people who are not Excel experts. You never compute or invent numbers: every figure you mention must already appear in the evidence you were given. You never claim something is wrong that the evidence does not state. Write plainly, in the second person, with no jargon and no exclamation marks.
